title: AlphaFold 2: Atomic-Accuracy Protein Structure Prediction (CASP14)
whyItMatters: Solved biology's 50-year protein structure prediction grand challenge at atomic accuracy—earning the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry and establishing the modern AI-for-science benchmark.
summary: Validated at the blind CASP14 competition in November 2020 and published in Nature (July 2021), DeepMind's AlphaFold 2 introduced the Evoformer and equivariant structure modules to predict 3D atomic coordinates of proteins directly from amino-acid sequences with accuracy rivaling X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM. Releasing open source code and >200 million predicted structures in the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database permanently transformed structural biology and served as the blueprint for the entire 2020s wave of scientific AI.
technicalHighlights: Achieved ~0.96 Å median backbone RMSD on blind CASP14 targets, effectively solving single-chain static protein folding.
Awarded half of the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry (Demis Hassabis and John Jumper).
Open-source release and EMBL-EBI database unlocked >200 million structures used by millions of researchers worldwide.
caveats: Predicts static single-chain conformations rather than dynamic conformational ensembles, multi-ligand complexes, or folding pathways—gaps subsequently targeted by AlphaFold 3 and generative biology models.

scoreRationale.foundational: Resolved a 50-year grand challenge in molecular biology and proved deep learning can crack core scientific physics problems.
scoreRationale.ripple: One of the highest-impact scientific tools of the 21st century—directly catalyzing AlphaFold 3, AlphaProteo, Evo 2, and modern drug discovery.
scoreRationale.verification: Blind CASP14 benchmark victory, landmark Nature paper, tens of thousands of independent experimental confirmations, and the 2024 Nobel Prize.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed months-to-years of crystallography per protein into minutes of computation.
